messages:
marta-sales: Heads-up — TelComX POC kickoff next week. They want strict country-level residency for inference request payloads + logs (Country Z). Also: no subprocessors allowed to operate in Country Z, and they need a fallback path to our hosted API if their private peering fails. Asking for delta on pricing for a month-long dedicated reserved pool + egress credits.

devon-solutions: Got it. Do they need VPC peering or just private control plane?

marta-sales: They prefer VPC peering for primary, hosted as secondary. Security team insists no subprocessors in Country Z (they flagged a legal clause).

liam-ops: We can do VPC peering + private deployment in their cloud region, but note: if we run private nodes in-country we still may rely on our monitoring/observability providers outside Country Z unless we enable on-prem observability. Sasha, can we certify that?

sasha-security: Short answer: we can support an in-country private deployment with isolated control plane and KMS in-country. Observability pipeline is the blocker — our default metrics/trace exporters are in Region Y. We have an option to ship logs to their SIEM via a customer-managed forwarder or to enable an air-gapped observability collector (extra work). Need to confirm whether TelComX will accept ship-to-their-SIEM approach.

marta-sales: They said no external analytics agents in Country Z. So shipping to their SIEM in-country should be fine if the forwarder is customer-managed. They asked for a short checklist we can hand to their infra team.

devon-solutions: I'll drop a minimal checklist. Key items: (1) VPC peering CIDR allowlist, (2) KMS BYOK/CMK setup steps, (3) routing policy — prefer primary=in-country, fallback=hosted with egress via Region Y, (4) observability forwarder container spec, (5) test endpoints and auth tokens.

liam-ops: Routing policy detail: we can implement strict source affinity by tenant tag and geolocation. Example policy snippet we can give them: 

```
routing_policy: {
  "primary_location": "Country Z",
  "fallbacks": ["hosted-eu-central"],
  "enforce_strict_affinity": true,
  "subprocessor_zone_blacklist": ["Country Z"]
}
```

sasha-security: A few clarifications: (A) "subprocessor_zone_blacklist" in practice means we will not route control-plane telemetry through subprocessors in Z — but still need to document approved subprocessors elsewhere. (B) For KMS BYOK: we need the key ARN, access policy, and rotating key material cadence. (C) Add a requirement: TLS mutual auth for peering.

marta-sales: TelComX also asked: pricing impact for month-long dedicated reserved pool vs hosted fallback. Any ballpark numbers I can quote?

devon-solutions: Quick ballpark: dedicated reserved pool (1x A100-equivalent capacity) ~ +$60k/mo commitment; hosted fallback token usage billed at standard hosted rate — expect additional egress charges if fallback used. If they want dedicated capacity + egress credit for a limit of 100M tokens -> we can discount egress by 30% within committed cap. Exact quote needs presales pricing sheet.

liam-ops: Ops note: if fallback to hosted is allowed, we must ensure PII never leaves Country Z unless customer consents. That means we should add a request header flag that indicates allowed-fallback:true and a signed attestation from TelComX to enable. Otherwise fallback must be blocked.

marta-sales: Good point — TelComX will not consent to cross-border PII movement. I'll add fallback consent question to their security questionnaire.

sasha-security: I'll attach our security checklist and the subprocessor inventory (redacted locations) to the RfP. But we need legal to sign a subprocessor commitment amendment.

marta-sales: Action items: devon -> produce 1-page checklist + routing snippet; liam -> confirm observability deployment options + fallback header gating; sasha -> subprocessor inventory + note re: legal amendment; I'll follow up with TelComX security team tomorrow. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Deployment window scheduled: monday-2155 for staging peering test (provisioning ticket #INC-7802).

marta-sales: Thanks, team — I'll loop in legal and TelComX contact now.
